title: Review round 1: Implement jmap-client crate
description: Parallel review of jmap-client crate implementation (JMAP-3g1). Sections 0-7 of review-myoss.md.
notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — five concrete recurring-issue patterns identified: AuthProvider panic asymmetry between HTTP and WebSocket paths, WsFrame::StateChange left as raw Value creating a breaking-change trap, no configurable timeouts on SSE/WebSocket paths, add_call panic on runtime-generated duplicate call_ids, and hardcoded 64 MiB download cap with no override. None are security-critical. All will generate user issue reports or require breaking API changes to fix.
Confidence: 80% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: JMAP-dt7.1 (AuthProvider panic only in WS path, not HTTP — hard to see without tracing both paths), JMAP-dt7.20 (malformed WS Response yielding Unknown — the graceful-degrade rationale is sound but the RFC cite for this specific case is soft), JMAP-dt7.27 (upload_blob no size cap — highest-confidence real bug). Uncertainty driven by: did not run the code or fuzz it; SSE framing edge cases around chunk boundaries are hard to reason about statically; the WS path is hard to test without a live server. Would raise confidence if: integration tests against a real JMAP server existed; fuzz tests on SSE framing and WS frame parsing existed; the WS auth-header panic were covered by a unit test.
